results.name: Barbell Seated Military Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with feet flat on the floor, back first in front of a rack. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Position the barbell in front of your shoulders, just below chin level.
Press the barbell overhead by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position with control by bending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell overhead and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
results.description: Barbell Seated Military Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

results.name: Barbell Seated Overhead Press
instructions: Sit on a bench with your feet flat on the floor. Hold a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Position the barbell at shoulder height in front of you.
Press the barbell overhead by extending your elbows until your arms are fully extended.
Lower the barbell back down to the starting position with control, bending your elbows.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell overhead and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Use a weight that allows for proper form and control throughout the exercise to prevent strain or injury.
results.description: Barbell Seated Overhead Press is a beginner multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

results.name: Barbell Shrugs
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. Let the barbell hang in front of your thighs.
Lift your shoulders straight up towards your ears as high as you can, keeping your arms straight.
Squeeze your upper back muscles (trapezius) at the top of the movement.
Lower your shoulders back down to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms straight throughout the movement to focus on your shoulder muscles.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
Avoid rotating your shoulders as you lift and lower them to prevent strain.
results.description: Barbell Shrugs is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Barbell Silverback Shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with both hands using an overhand grip (palms down). Your hands should be shoulder-width apart. Bend your knees slightly and hinge forward at the hips, keeping your back straight and your torso at 45 degrees to the ground.
Start with your arms fully extended, letting the barbell hang directly below your shoulders.
Shrug your shoulders upward to your ears. Focus on squeezing your shoulder blades together at the top of the movement.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position. Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions.
tips: Maintain a neutral spine and avoid rounding your back during the exercise to prevent injury.
Engage your core to stabilize your torso and maintain balance throughout the movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you shrug your shoulders upward and inhaling as you lower them back down.
results.description: Barbell Silverback Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Barbell Standing Close Grip Military Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), hands placed at shoulder-width apart. The barbell should be at chest height.
Press the barbell overhead by extending your arms fully, making sure to keep the bar path straight and close to your body.
Hold the barbell overhead for a moment and slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position at chest height. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid arching your back by maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell overhead and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Keep your elbows slightly in front of your body at the starting position to avoid shoulder strain.
results.description: Barbell Standing Close Grip Military Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps.

results.name: Barbell Standing Military Press

Press the barbell overhead by extending your arms fully, making sure to keep the bar path straight and close to your body.
Hold the barbell overhead for a moment, ensuring your arms are fully extended and your shoulders are engaged.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position at chest height. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid arching your back by maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell overhead and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Keep your elbows slightly in front of your body at the starting position to avoid shoulder strain.
results.description: Barbell Standing Military Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest.

results.name: Barbell Standing Shoulder Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), hands placed slightly wider than shoulder-width apart. The barbell should be at chest height.
Press the barbell overhead by extending your arms fully, keeping your elbows outwards.
Hold the barbell overhead for a moment, ensuring your arms are fully extended and your shoulders are engaged.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position at chest height. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid arching your back by maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell overhead and inhaling as you lower it back down.
Keep your elbows slightly in front of your body at the starting position to avoid shoulder strain.
results.description: Barbell Standing Shoulder Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest.

results.name: Barbell Standing Wide Grip Military Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing forward), hands placed 2 fists wider than shoulder-width apart. The barbell should be at chest height.
Press the barbell overhead by extending your arms fully, making sure to keep the bar path straight and close to your body.
Hold the barbell overhead for a moment, ensuring your arms are fully extended and your shoulders are engaged.
Slowly lower the barbell back to the starting position at chest height. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid arching your back by maintaining a neutral spine throughout the movement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the barbell overhead and inhaling as you lower it back down.

results.name: Barbell Wide Shrug
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a barbell with an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands placed wider than shoulder-width apart. Allow the barbell to rest against your thighs with your arms fully extended.
Raise your shoulders towards your ears as high as possible, keeping your arms straight and the barbell close to your body.
Hold the contraction at the top for a moment, squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Slowly lower your shoulders back to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your arms straight and avoid using your biceps to lift the barbell.
Focus on using your trapezius muscles to lift your shoulders, not your arms.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you lift your shoulders and inhaling as you lower them back down.
results.description: Barbell Wide Shrug is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the traps (back). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Barbell Z Press
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended and your feet slightly apart. Hold the barbell at shoulder height using an overhand grip (palms facing forward), slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your back straight, engage your core, and ensure your chest is upright.
Press the barbell overhead by extending your arms fully, keeping your head neutral and looking forward.
Slowly lower the barbell back to shoulder height. Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions.
tips: Engage your core to stabilize your torso and maintain an upright posture.
Use a controlled motion to lift and lower the barbell to maximize shoulder engagement.
Breathe steadily, exhaling as you press the bar up and inhaling as you lower it back down.
results.description: Barbell Z Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Triceps, Core.
